title: KPI Orbit Mapping and Incident Playbook
body:
Context and intent:
This doc is a short, pragmatic working artifact to: (1) map our launch KPIs into a phased 'orbit' view so engineers and ops can see which signals matter at each cadence; (2) provide explicit acceptance/rollback triggers for canary and full rollout; (3) include a compact incident playbook focused on launch-specific degradations (latency, token-cost spikes, quality regressions).

Why 'orbit' mapping?
- Many launch signal documents list metrics in one place and operations runbooks in another. The orbit model groups metrics into concentric phases: preflight, canary, ramp, steady-state. Each phase has different owners, thresholds, and remediation playbooks.

Quick TL;DR (for ops lead)
- Canary window: 1–4 hours, 1% traffic -> monitor p99 latency, failed-request-rate, token-cost-per-response, QoQ model-quality score.
- Canary abort if p99 > 1.5x baseline OR failed-request-rate > 0.5% sustained 5m OR token-cost spike > 2x expected for two consecutive 5m windows.
- Ramp step: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 30m between steps and automated rollback on repeated signal breaches.

Orbit phases and core signals (owner in parens):
1) Preflight (product-ops / release engineers)
   - Smoke: model loaded, endpoint responds (healthcheck)
   - Baseline telemetry: p50/p90/p99 latency for 512-token responses
   - Cost profile: avg tokens per request, token-cost-per-req estimate
   - QA quality pass rate against canary prompt set (local eval harness)
   - Acceptance: all smoke green + QA pass >= 95%

2) Canary (oncall + release engineer)
   - Traffic: 1% user traffic or synthetic load representative of key personas
   - Latency signals: p99, p90, p50 (owner: infra)
   - Errors: failed-response-rate, model-timeouts (owner: s-reliability)
   - Cost and throughput: tokens/sec, egress costs (owner: finance-eng)
   - Quality: canary prompt-set accuracy + hallucination rate (owner: product-research)
   - Canary abort triggers (automated):
     * p99 > 1.5x preflight baseline for 2 consecutive windows (5m windows)
     * failed-response-rate > 0.5% sustained over 5m
     * canary-quality drop >= 6 percentage points vs baseline on core prompts
     * token-cost-per-response > 2x estimate for 10m

3) Ramp (release lead + infra)
   - Step increases at 10% -> 50% -> 100% (30m minimum between steps unless manually overridden)
   - Watchlist: rolling 30m error-rate, latency trend slope, resource saturation (GPU mem/SM util)
   - Auto throttle rule: if any of the nine watchlist signals crosses threshold twice within an hour, pause ramp and escalate

4) Steady-state (product-ops + SRE + billing)
   - Long-term KPIs: cost per 1k tokens, daily active users served, SLA compliance (uptime and p99 latency), regression on prompt-set quality
   - Monthly review triggers: weekly quality drift > 2% triggers model-re-eval and potential rollback to prior variant

Compact KPI tracker (what to record every 5m during canary/ramp)
- timestamp
- traffic %
- p50, p90, p99 latencies (ms)
- failed-resp-rate (%)
- avg tokens per response
- token-cost-per-response (USD)
- canary-quality-score (0-100) on sampled prompts
- owner notes (free text)

Acceptance criteria (small checklist)
- [ ] Healthchecks stable for 10 minutes
- [ ] Canary QA >= 95% on core prompts
- [ ] p99 within 1.2x baseline
- [ ] Billing estimate within 10% of projected
- [ ] No memory/GPU OOM observed

Rollback and escalation decision tree (short)
- Immediate abort conditions (stop and rollback to previous model):
  * Major latency outage: p99 > 2x baseline for 10m AND customer-facing errors observed
  * Quality catastrophic: canary-quality drop > 15 points AND user-visible failures in prod samples
  * Cost runaway: token-cost-per-response > 3x estimate for 15m
- If any of the above: Release lead triggers rollback, oncall pages SRE, product-ops opens incident.
- If borderline signals (e.g., minor quality drop, small latency increase): pause ramp, run focused replay against last-good checkpoint, open a triage Slack thread #launch-room and invite product-ops + applied-ml.

Incident playbook (first 60 minutes)
1) Triage (owner: oncall)
   - Snapshot last 30m metrics (KPI tracker)
   - Collect 5 representative failed requests and model responses
   - Check GPU/host-level metrics (util, memory, network)
2) Containment (owner: SRE)
   - If latency/errors high: enable automatic fallback route to prior smaller model (if configured) OR reduce concurrency cap for serving pool
   - If cost spike: enact temporary request-sampling (sample 10% of noisy endpoints) and notify billing ops
3) Root-cause (owner: applied-ml + infra)
   - Run local eval of canary prompts against deployed binary/artifact and prior artifact; compare outputs
   - If regression found in model outputs: revert to previous model artifact
4) Communication (owner: release lead)
   - Post interim status every 15 minutes to #launch-room and update the incident ticket (JIRA-PROD-<id>)

Notes / unresolved items (TO-DOs)
- Need a lightweight dashboard tile that computes token-cost-per-response in real-time for canary (ask console team, PR referenced above).
- Confirm whether 'automatic fallback to quantized variant' is safe for the specific release (Marco to sign off).
- Add one synthetic story per core persona to the canary set (product-research).

Runbook snippets worth copying into alert rules (searchable keywords):
- "canary_p99_regression" -> alert when p99 > 1.5x baseline over 2 windows
- "canary_quality_delta" -> alert when sample-quality delta >= 6 points
- "token_cost_spike" -> alert when rolling 10m median token-cost-per-req > 2x projection

Quick links and artifacts
- Canary prompt set (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/canary-prompts
- Rollout PR: https://github.com/redwood/console/pull/412
- Incident template (jira): JIRA-PROD-3841

Final notes (notes-to-self style)
- Keep this doc short and focused; the large canonical runbook lives in SRE playbooks. This is the transitory, launch-focused companion that maps metrics to decisions in a readable orbit format.
- After the release, capture a short 1-page retrospective: what signals were helpful, which thresholds were too tight/too loose, and any missing correlates (e.g., NLB queue length).

-- Aisha
